referral.merchant_message: Busy match day, one expired card declined.

steps.text: I'll start by looking up the merchant, the transaction, and any earlier referrals — all in parallel.
Good — I now have the merchant and transaction details, and there are no earlier referrals. Next, I'll screen the merchant name and owner against sanctions, and check the card status.

Here's my assessment of all the checks:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Sanctions – merchant** | Score 0.55 — well below 0.85, clear |
| **Sanctions – owner** | Score 0.28 — well below 0.85, clear |
| **Card status** | Active (expiry 2027-09) |
| **Amount** | £64.00 — under £5,000 threshold |
| **Days trading** | 915 — well over 30 |
| **Duplicate referral** | No earlier referrals |
| **Complaint language** | None detected |

The decline reason is clearly "card expired," returned by the issuing bank. Interestingly, our records show the card token as active, which may mean the issuer has reissued a replacement card while the old details were used for this transaction. This is a straightforward issuer-side decline with a specific reason. I'll resolve with guidance.

input.message_to_merchant: Thank you for getting in touch. The payment was declined by the card issuer with the reason "card expired." Please ask your customer to check whether a replacement card has been issued and to retry the payment using their updated card details. If the problem persists, the customer should contact their bank directly.
